cardsNote: Draft reference, last reviewed Nov 2026. Rates change: always copy the VAT/tax amount printed on the receipt and use these cards only as a sanity check.

modules.title: Vendor
modules.summary: Which business name to type, and which names to ignore.

lesson.p: The vendor is the business that sold the item or service. It is the name customers see at the top of the receipt.
ul: Use the trading name printed at the top (for example 'Starbucks'), not the card brand (Visa), the payment app, or the cashier's name.
Do not add store numbers, branch codes or slogans unless they are part of the business name.
If you only see a logo, look at the footer or website line for the written name.
Ride-hailing and delivery: the vendor is the platform (Grab, Uber, Careem), not the driver.

modules.bis: The vendor is the business that sold the item. Not the card (Visa), not the cashier, and not the driver.

quiz.q: The logo says 'STARBUCKS COFFEE'. The footer says 'Operated by Smith Hospitality LLC · Store #4412'. What is the vendor?
quiz.why: Use the trading name customers see at the top. The operator company and store number are extra details.

quiz.q: A Grab receipt says 'Thanks for riding with Grab' and shows the driver name 'Juan D.'. What is the vendor?
quiz.why: For ride-hailing the vendor is the platform, not the driver.

quiz.q: A card slip shows 'VISA APPROVED' and merchant 'THE LOCAL PUB'. What is the vendor?
quiz.why: The card brand only shows how it was paid.

quiz.q: Should you add the store number (like '#0412') to the vendor name?
o: No, only if it is part of the business name
quiz.why: Store numbers are not part of the name unless the business uses them as its name.

modules.title: Receipt size
modules.rule: Ask your admin for the exact Small / Medium / Large rule used by Abukai. (Admin: write the rule here in training-data.json, module 'size', field 'rule'.)

lesson.p: Receipt size is a dropdown with three choices: Small, Medium, Large.
ul: Pick the size that matches the paper or image of the receipt as shown in the portal.
Always follow the exact rule from Abukai guidelines. When in doubt, ask your admin.
Do not change the size to match the category or the amount.

modules.bis: Small, Medium or Large: follow Abukai's exact rule. If you are not sure, ask the admin.

modules.title: Category
modules.summary: Meals, lodging, airfare, parking, supplies and all the others.

lesson.h: Choose by what the money was spent on
lesson.p: Pick the category from the main item bought, not from the type of shop.
ul: Meals: restaurants, cafes, fast food, drinks.
Lodging: hotel, hostel, apartment stays (a hotel bill is Lodging).
Airfare: airline tickets.
Taxi / Rideshare: taxi, Grab, Uber, Lyft, Careem.
Mileage: distance driven in miles or km, usually from a log or map, not a shop receipt.
Parking: garages, meters, valet.
Fuel: gas, petrol, diesel.
Tolls: toll roads and bridges.
Supplies: office items, stationery, small purchases for work.
Other: only when nothing above fits.
A gas-station receipt that is mostly fuel is Fuel, even if there is a snack on it.
A hotel bill with breakfast is Lodging. Split out meals only if your guideline says so.
Use the category list in the portal. If the portal list differs from this one, the portal wins.

modules.bis: Choose the category by what was bought, not by the type of shop.

quiz.q: A receipt from 'Heathrow Airport Car Park' for 3 days. Category?
quiz.why: It is a fee for leaving a car: Parking.

quiz.q: A hotel bill shows 2 nights of room and one breakfast. Category?
quiz.why: A hotel bill is Lodging. Split out meals only if your guideline says so.

quiz.q: A gas-station receipt: fuel 40.00 and a bag of chips 2.50. Category?
quiz.why: Choose by the main item. The fuel is almost the whole amount.

quiz.q: An Uber ride receipt. Category?
quiz.why: Rides in Uber, Grab, Lyft or Careem are Taxi / Rideshare.

quiz.q: A receipt from an office-supply store for paper and pens. Category?
quiz.why: Office items are Supplies.

quiz.q: An airline e-ticket receipt Manila to Singapore. Category?
quiz.why: An airline ticket is Airfare.

modules.title: City, State & Country
modules.summary: Read addresses from different countries correctly.

ul: City: the town or city printed in the address.
State: the state, province or region (US: two letters such as IL = Illinois; Canada: ON, BC, QC).
Country: from the address. If it is missing, combine clues: currency, phone code (+49 Germany, +63 Philippines, +971 UAE), tax words (GST, MwSt, TVA), language.

lesson.h: Address order is not the same everywhere
ul: Germany, France, Spain, Italy: postal code comes BEFORE the city (10557 Berlin).
UK: the postcode comes after the city (London SW1E 5DH).
US: city, state, then ZIP code (Chicago, IL 60603).
Japan writes the address from the big area to the small one (prefecture, city, ward).

lesson.p: If the clues disagree and you cannot decide, ask your admin. A wrong country also gives a wrong date and amount format.

modules.bis: Use the postal code, not the city. If there is no address, use the currency, phone code and tax words.

quiz.q: Address: '10557 Berlin, Germany'. Which part is the city?
quiz.why: 10557 is the postal code. In Germany it comes before the city.

quiz.q: Address: 'Springfield, IL 62704, USA'. What is the state?
quiz.why: In the US the two letters after the city are the state.

quiz.q: A receipt has no address, but shows CAD, a +1 416 phone number and 'HST 13%'. Country?
quiz.why: CAD, HST and a Toronto area code all point to Canada.

quiz.q: The address clearly says Madrid, Spain, but you also see a US dollar sign. What do you do?
o: Use the printed address (Spain) and ask admin if still unsure
quiz.why: The printed address is the strongest clue. Ask instead of guessing.

modules.title: Date
modules.summary: Read the right date in the right order for each country.

ul: 1) Find the transaction date: purchase, service or invoice date. Not the print date, not the due date, not a loyalty-offer date.
2) Find the country of the receipt (see module 4).
3) Read the numbers in that country's order, then enter the date as the portal needs.
US: month / day / year, so 03/04/2026 is 4 March 2026.
UK, most of Europe, Australia, India, Singapore, UAE: day / month / year, so 03/04/2026 is 3 April 2026.
Germany, Switzerland, Poland, Turkey use dots: 03.04.2026 is 3 April 2026.
China, Japan, Korea, Sweden: year first (2026-03-07 or 2026年3月7日).
Philippines: many receipts use month / day / year, some use day / month / year. Check other clues.
If the first or second number is bigger than 12 (for example 26/03/2026 or 03/26/2026), it must be the day. That tells you the order.
Two-digit year: 20.05.26 means 2026.
Thailand uses the Buddhist Era: subtract 543 (2569 is 2026).
Taiwan uses the ROC year: add 1911 (115 is 2026).
Japan may use the Reiwa era: Reiwa 8 is 2026.
Saudi Arabia may print Hijri dates. Use the Gregorian date.
Month names change by language: März, mars, marzo, março and maart all mean March; mei means May; ene means January in Spanish.

modules.bis: Find the country first, then follow its date order. If a number is above 12, that number is the day.

quiz.q: Receipt from Chicago, USA shows 03/04/2026. Which date is it?
quiz.why: The US uses month / day / year: 03 = March, 04 = day.

quiz.q: Receipt from London, UK shows 03/04/2026. Which date is it?
quiz.why: The UK uses day / month / year: 3 April.

quiz.q: Receipt from Berlin shows 03.04.2026. Which date is it?
quiz.why: Germany uses day.month.year.

quiz.q: A receipt shows 26/03/2026 and you do not know the country. Which date?
quiz.why: 26 cannot be a month, so the order is day / month.

quiz.q: A Tokyo receipt shows 2026年3月7日. Which date?
quiz.why: Japanese dates go year, month (月), day (日): 7 March 2026.

quiz.q: A Bangkok receipt shows 12/03/2569. Which date?
quiz.why: Thai Buddhist Era is 543 years ahead: 2569 − 543 = 2026. Thailand uses day / month.

quiz.q: A European receipt shows 'Printed: 15/11/2026' and 'Date of service: 12/11/2026'. Which date do you enter?
quiz.why: Use the transaction date, not the print date, unless your guideline says otherwise.

quiz.q: A Manila receipt shows 11/14/2026. Which date?
quiz.why: Many Philippine receipts use month / day / year. 14 cannot be a month, so it confirms the order.

modules.title: Amount & currency

ul: Enter the final total charged (after tax). Not the subtotal, not the cash given, not the change.
Enter the currency printed on the receipt. A $ sign alone can be USD, CAD, AUD, SGD or MXN: use the country.
1,234.56: US, UK, Philippines, Australia, Singapore, Japan, China, Thailand, UAE.
1.234,56: Germany, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Brazil, Turkey, Indonesia.
1 234,56 (space): France, Sweden, Poland, Czech Republic.
1'234.56: Switzerland.
1,23,456.78: India (lakh grouping: the first group has three digits, the next groups two).
The LAST separator is usually the decimal one, with 2 digits after it.
Yen (JPY), Korean won (KRW) and Vietnamese dong (VND) have no decimals. Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman use 3 decimals.
A German '1.500' with EUR is 1500.00, because euros have only 2 decimals.
In the practice tool, type the amount with a dot for decimals and no thousand separators, like 1234.56.

modules.bis: The last dot or comma is usually the decimal. In Germany, 1.234,56 = 1234.56.

quiz.q: A German receipt shows 1.234,56 €. What is the amount?
quiz.why: In Germany the dot groups thousands and the comma is the decimal.

quiz.q: A German receipt shows 'EUR 1.500'. What is the amount?
quiz.why: Euros have 2 decimals, so three digits after the dot means thousands.

quiz.q: A French receipt shows 1 234,50 €. What is the amount?
quiz.why: France groups thousands with a space and uses a comma for decimals.

quiz.q: A Swiss receipt shows CHF 1'250.00. What is the amount?
quiz.why: The apostrophe groups thousands in Switzerland.

quiz.q: An Indian receipt shows ₹1,23,456.00. What is the amount?
quiz.why: Indian lakh grouping: 1,23,456 is one hundred twenty-three thousand four hundred fifty-six.

quiz.q: A Tokyo receipt shows ¥1,080. What do you enter?
quiz.why: Yen has no decimals. The comma only groups thousands.

quiz.q: Subtotal 44.98, tax 4.61, total 49.59, cash 60.00, change 10.41. Which amount?
quiz.why: Enter the final total charged.

quiz.q: A receipt from Sydney shows a $ sign. Which currency?
quiz.why: The symbol alone is ambiguous. Sydney is in Australia, so AUD.

modules.title: VAT / tax
modules.summary: Find the VAT amount when the country has one.

lesson.p: VAT (Value Added Tax) is a tax already included in the price in most countries outside the US. It has different names.
ul: VAT, GST, MwSt (Germany), TVA (France), IVA (Spain, Italy), BTW (Netherlands), MOMS (Nordic), PPN (Indonesia), KDV (Turkey), consumption tax (Japan).
The US and Canada's provinces use sales tax added at checkout. The US has no VAT.

lesson.h: How to fill the VAT field
ul: Copy the VAT amount printed on the receipt. Do not calculate it from memory.
If only the rate and the total are shown, VAT included in the total = total × rate ÷ (100 + rate). Example: 18.00 at 20% → 18.00 × 20 ÷ 120 = 3.00.
If the receipt shows no tax at all, leave VAT empty (or 0 if the portal needs a number). Never invent a number.
The VAT amount uses the same currency as the total.
If a receipt has two rates (for example 7% and 19% in Germany), follow your guideline on whether to enter each line or the sum. Ask admin if unsure.

lesson.p: The Country cards list the usual VAT name and standard rate. Use them to sanity-check what you read, never to replace the amount on the receipt.

modules.bis: Copy the VAT printed on the receipt. Do not invent it. If there is no tax, leave VAT empty.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a name for a VAT-style tax?
quiz.why: A tip is a gratuity, not a tax.

quiz.q: A German receipt shows 'MwSt 19%  2,00'. What VAT amount do you enter?
quiz.why: Enter the VAT amount (2.00), not the rate.

quiz.q: A UK parking receipt shows Total £18.00 and 'VAT 20%' but no VAT amount. What is the VAT amount?
quiz.why: The price includes VAT: 18.00 × 20 ÷ 120 = 3.00.

quiz.q: A US receipt shows 'Sales tax 4.61'. What about the VAT field?
o: The US has no VAT, so leave it empty unless your guideline says otherwise
quiz.why: The US uses sales tax, not VAT.

quiz.q: The receipt shows no tax line at all. What do you do?
quiz.why: Only enter VAT you can read or calculate from the receipt.

quiz.q: A Japanese receipt shows '内消費税10% ¥98'. What VAT amount do you enter?
quiz.why: Japan's consumption tax is its VAT. The amount included is ¥98.

modules.title: Description

ul: Say what was bought: 'Lunch for 2 people', 'Airport parking, 3 days', 'Taxi from hotel to office'.
Use details visible on the receipt: number of nights, number of people, route, items.
Keep it short and factual. No opinions and no business reasons that are not on the receipt.
Check your spelling. Use English unless the guideline says otherwise.

modules.bis: Keep it short and factual: what was bought. No opinions.

quiz.q: A café receipt shows 1 coffee and 2 pretzels. Which description is best?
quiz.why: It says exactly what was bought.

quiz.q: A Careem receipt in Dubai. Which description is best?
o: Careem Dubai paid by card thanks
quiz.why: It is short, factual, and shows type and place.

quiz.q: What should a description NOT include?
o: Number of nights for a hotel
quiz.why: Do not add information that is not on the receipt.

practice.tip: Germany: day.month.year, decimal comma. MwSt is VAT, and the printed VAT amount is 2,00.
US: month/day/year, so 03/04/2026 is 4 March. Sales tax is not VAT, so VAT stays empty. The amount is the total, not the cash.
France: day/month/year, so 05/11 is 5 November. A space groups thousands. TVA is VAT. A hotel bill is Lodging.
India: lakh grouping, so 1,23,456.00 is 123456.00. GST is the VAT-type tax. 14 cannot be a month, so the date is 14 February.
Japan: year, month, day. Yen has no decimals. 内消費税 means consumption tax included, ¥98.
Many Philippine receipts use month/day/year. 14 cannot be a month, so it is 14 November. VAT 12% is 26.25.
UK: day/month/year, so 07/03 is 7 March. The VAT amount printed is £3.00.
A written month name removes any confusion. Careem is a ride-hailing platform, so the category is Taxi / Rideshare.
Switzerland: day.month.year, so 5.11 is 5 November. The apostrophe groups thousands. MWST is VAT.
Thailand uses the Buddhist Era: 2569 − 543 = 2026. Day/month/year, so 12 March 2026.

countries.tax: Sales tax (state/local, added at checkout). No VAT.

countries.d: DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD: check clues
countries.tax: GST 5%; HST 13-15% in some provinces; PST/QST in others
Taxes are built into prices; the receipt may not show a clear VAT line

countries.d: DD/MM/YYYY (Gregorian). Hijri dates may also be printed

countries.tax: GST: mostly 5% or 18% slabs (check the receipt)

countries.d: MM/DD/YYYY is common; DD/MM/YYYY also seen

countries.tax: SST (sales tax 5-10%, service tax 6-8%). Not VAT

countries.d: YYYY/MM/DD or YYYY年M月D日; Reiwa era (R8 = 2026) can appear
